# Archer Lodge Labradors

> Family-raised English Labrador Retriever breeder on Archer Lodge Rd in Clayton, North Carolina (Johnston County, just east of Raleigh). Owned by Abigail Valletta and family, breeding since 2019. AKC registered, genetically tested parents; puppies raised in the home with the family's children. Also offers stud service and nationwide ground and air puppy transport.

## Key facts
- Business: Archer Lodge Labradors (also "Archer Lodge Labs")
- Owner: Abigail Valletta
- Breed: English-type Labrador Retrievers — yellow, black, chocolate, some champagne; imports from Serbia and Poland
- Address: Archer Lodge Rd, Clayton, NC 27527, United States
- Phone (call or text): (919) 899-8917
- Email: archerlodgelabpups@gmail.com
- Visits: by appointment only
- Puppy price: $3,500–$5,500 depending on the pedigree of the pairing; full AKC registration offered on a limited basis at the higher end
- Deposit: $500, non-refundable, holds a place on the waiting list and goes toward the price
- Payment accepted: Cash, Zelle, Venmo, PayPal, cashier's check, credit card, Apple Pay, Cash App
- Included with each puppy: AKC registration, microchip, deworming, first set of shots, a toy and a blanket that smells like the litter; parents' genetics and pedigree on request
- Health: all breeding dogs AKC registered with completed genetic testing; many OFA hip/elbow evaluated, cleared by parentage, or under evaluation
- Transport: ground $2 per mile round trip; air $850–$2,000 depending on flight and distance; ships anywhere in the US
- Stud service: to approved AKC-registered, genetically tested females; studs include Victor, Moose, Sir Knox and Nolan Jacob
- Dams: Bailey Girl, Mila Bear, Lana Del Rey, Aśka Willow
- Google rating: 5.0 (Google reviews) — review link: https://g.page/r/Cap9abCvWZLDEAE/review
- Areas served: Archer Lodge, Clayton, Smithfield, Selma, Garner, Raleigh, Knightdale, Wendell, Zebulon, Wake Forest, Cary, Apex, Holly Springs, Fuquay-Varina, Durham, Chapel Hill, Goldsboro, Wilson, Rocky Mount and all of North Carolina; nationwide via transport
- Social: https://www.facebook.com/archerlodgelabs/ · https://www.instagram.com/archerlodgelabradors · https://www.x.com/ArcherLodgeLabs

## Top questions
- **How much are your puppies?** Puppies run $3,500 to $5,500 depending on the dam's and stud's pedigree — the full breakdown is on the pricing page.
- **What do your puppies come with?** AKC registration, a microchip, deworming, and their first set of shots. Every pup also goes home with a toy and a blanket that smells like their litter.
- **Why do prices vary between litters?** Price depends on the pedigree of the mother and father. Litters from our imported, fully English lines with full AKC registration available sit at the higher end of the range.
- **Does the price change over time?** Prices can shift with the economy, but we always try to keep them fair and reasonable for our families. The price you're quoted when you reserve is the one we honor.
- **What payment methods do you accept?** We accept cash, Zelle, Venmo, PayPal, cashier's checks, credit cards, Apple Pay and Cash App. Deposits and payments are arranged directly with us.
- **Are males and females priced differently?** Pricing is set by the pairing, not the sex of the puppy. Call or text and we'll tell you exactly what a pup from a given litter costs.
- **What colors do your puppies come in?** We raise yellow, black and chocolate English Labradors, and some pairings can produce champagne. Each litter's expected colors are listed on the available puppies page.
- **Do you have puppies available right now?** Our current puppies and open litters are always on the available puppies page. It's updated as pups are reserved, so call or text to confirm who is still looking for a home.
- **How big will my English Lab get?** Our adult girls range from about 55 to 81 pounds, and English Labs tend to be stockier than American Labs. Your puppy's adult size will fall close to its parents'.
- **Do you donate any of the proceeds?** Yes. With each litter we donate a portion of the proceeds to charities close to our hearts. It's our way of sharing the joy these dogs bring us.
- **How do I reserve a puppy?** Call or text (919) 899-8917, or email us, and tell us a little about your family and what you're hoping for. A deposit holds your spot. Our waiting list fills quickly, so the earlier you reach out the better.
- **How much is the deposit?** A $500 deposit holds your place in line for a current or upcoming litter. The deposit goes toward the price of your puppy.
- **Is the deposit refundable?** No. The $500 deposit is non-refundable, because holding your spot means turning other families away. If something comes up, talk to us and we'll do our best to help.
- **How does the waiting list work?** Families are placed in the order their deposits come in. As the puppies grow, we pick in that order, with our guidance on temperament to help you choose.
- **Can I pick my own puppy?** Yes. We watch every puppy's temperament closely and help you choose the one who fits your home, needs and preferences. Most families find our input on personality as helpful as the photos.
- **How do I pay the balance?** The remaining balance is due before or at pickup, using any of the payment methods we accept. We'll confirm the exact amount and timing when you reserve.
- **Can I reserve from out of state?** Absolutely. Many of our families live out of state and reserve by phone, then we arrange ground or air transport. You'll get photos and updates as your puppy grows.
- **Is there any cost to ask questions first?** None at all. There's no cost and no pressure in starting the conversation — we answer every call and text ourselves.
- **What do you want to know about my family?** Tell us about your home, kids, other pets, yard and schedule, and what you're hoping for in a Lab. It helps us match the right puppy to your life.
- **How far ahead should I get on the list?** As early as you can. Our litters often fill before the puppies are born, so reaching out a few months ahead gives you the best choice.
